themes.theme: Fed hawkish pivot after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech -- September 16 hike now live
themes.counter: Three FOMC members already dissented for a hike in July while the committee majority held; August CPI (due Sep 11, just before the meeting) could still come in soft and deflate hike odds, and some economists remain unconvinced Warsh's rhetoric becomes an actual vote

themes.theme: Iran conflict re-escalation driving an energy-price and inflation-risk shock (WTI +11.6% in a month, European gas at a 3-year high)
themes.counter: Prior 2026 Iran-conflict oil spikes have partially unwound once fighting paused; Strait of Hormuz has not actually closed, and research estimates the inflation pass-through is modest (+0.6pp headline) unless a full closure persists for a full quarter or more

themes.theme: AI capex boom still the market's central growth narrative, with hyperscaler spending guided sharply higher again
themes.counter: Capex-fatigue and monetization-timeline questions are building; top-10 S&P 500 concentration (35%) now exceeds the dot-com peak (25%), and momentum/quality factors (proxies for the AI trade) lagged value and high-beta over the last month

themes.theme: Narrowing short-term market breadth beneath a still-strong index level
themes.counter: The long-term breadth reading (>70% of names above their 200-day average) remains healthy by historical standards, so this may just be a rotation/consolidation rather than the start of a real breakdown

themes.theme: Fiscal-cliff risk temporarily defused: continuing resolution funds the government only through December 11, 2026
themes.counter: The CR passed with large bipartisan margins (House 370-48) and only 3 of 12 appropriations bills remain outstanding, suggesting a lower-drama path to full-year funding than the prior shutdown episode

regime_read.long_duration: With the Fed's easing cycle stalled and a hike now live for September while real 10-year yields sit above 2.4%, long-duration growth equities face a rising discount-rate headwind rather than the multiple-expansion tailwind of the prior easing narrative.
regime_read.cash_flow: Investment-grade and high-yield spreads remain historically tight (0.81% and 2.65% OAS) even as Treasury yields rose, so cash-generative names still borrow and refinance cheaply on a spread basis, but the ~5.4% single-A yield hurdle is high enough that only clearly compounding cash-flow stories clear it comfortably.
regime_read.small_caps: Small caps (IWM) are lagging large caps over the last month despite a strong 3-month stretch and a jobs report that argues against imminent recession, so the setup is rate-path dependent: a confirmed September hike would extend the underperformance, while a dovish surprise or soft August CPI could reignite the small-cap catch-up trade.
